land.text: Madura, from which the rebel army crossed, and the northern coastal towns of Mataram

predecessors.note: Not a state's successor: the rebels took Mataram land by force; Madura was a Mataram dependency of the Madurese prince Trunajaya.

land.text: Kediri, the rebels' last base, which fell on 25 November 1678

successors.note: Trunajaya himself held out until he 'surrendered to the VOC on 26 December 1679'; he held no land after Kediri.

capitals.name: Surabaya
capitals.note: 'In April 1677 the fleet sailed to Surabaya, where Trunajaya was based.' The page dates no earlier move; the coordinates are the modern city.

capitals.name: Kediri
capitals.note: The royal treasury 'went with the rebels to Kediri' after Plered fell in June 1677; Kediri fell on 25 November 1678.

correction.text: Madura and the northern coastal towns from Surabaya to the Cirebon border, Jepara excepted: rebels took most northern coastal towns, from Surabaya to Cirebon, except Jepara (the page, 1676-1677)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives no boundary; the coast is a union of 25-40 km circles round Surabaya, Tuban, Demak, Pati, Semarang and Tegal, and Madura a chain of circles. Cirebon, which the page has declare independence with Banten's support in 1677-1678, is not included.

correction.text: Kediri, to which the royal treasury was taken after the fall of Plered in June 1677 and where the rebels held out until 25 November 1678

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page does not say what became of Madura and the other coast towns after Surabaya fell in April 1677; they are dropped at confidence 1 in the ledger. (Reviewer se-02-g, 2026-10-19: the page does say VOC forces took Madura after the Surabaya campaign; ledger 3 is now confidence 2.)

region.text: Madura, from which 'a rebel army of 9,000' crossed to Java in September 1676

ledger.note: September 1676 (no month stored, so that the undated coast sweep can follow in order): Trunajaya's army crosses from Madura and routs the royal force at Gegodog. 'In September 1676, a rebel army of 9,000' crossed over and later took Surabaya; the first raid had been repulsed at Gresik in 1674 and Trunajaya had allied with the Kraeng of Galesong in 1675.

region.text: the northern coastal towns from Surabaya to Cirebon, Jepara excepted

ledger.note: 1676-1677: the rebels take the Java north coast. the page has rebels take most northern coastal towns, from Surabaya to Cirebon, except Jepara; the lord of Giri had joined the rebellion in early 1676. The page dates the sweep only as 1676-1677.

region.text: Kediri, where the treasury was taken

ledger.note: 1677: Kediri becomes the rebel base. The page dates only the treasury's move there (June 1677) and the fall of Kediri (25 November 1678).

region.text: Madura and the north-coast towns other than Surabaya

ledger.note: 1677: Madura and the remaining coast towns pass out of rebel hands. The page has, after the April 1677 Surabaya campaign, 'VOC forces also took Madura, Trunajaya's native island, and laid his residence there in ruin'; it does not name the other coast towns, which are not rebel-held after Surabaya fell, with Kediri the base by June 1677. (Reviewer se-02-g, 2026-10-19: confidence raised from 1 to 2 on the Madura sentence.)
April 1677: a VOC fleet under Cornelis Speelman takes Surabaya. 'In April 1677 the fleet sailed to Surabaya, where Trunajaya was based'; Trunajaya fled and Surabaya fell to VOC and Mataram forces.

region.text: the Mataram capital Plered, taken in mid-1677

ledger.note: June 1677: the rebels take Plered. The king, ill, fled west and the royal treasury went with the rebels to Kediri; Amangkurat I died at Tegal in July.

1677, entered at 1678: the rebels lose Plered to Pangeran Puger. The page: Puger 'had taken the old capital in Plered and had claimed the throne for himself in 1677', after the rebels withdrew to Kediri with the treasury in June 1677. No month is given, so the event is placed at 1678 to keep it after the June capture: a bridge. (Reviewer se-02-g, 2026-10-19: the page dates this to 1677, not 1677-1678; confidence lowered from 2 to 1.)
25 November 1678: Kediri falls to VOC and Mataram forces under François Tack. the page has Kediri fall on 25 November 1678, after the three-column march of September-November.

November 1678: the rebel state is crushed. Trunajaya fled, was beaten at Mlambang in 1679 and 'surrendered to the VOC on 26 December 1679'; Amangkurat II personally stabbed the captive Trunajaya at Payak in 1680 (the page, year only).

wars.name: Trunajaya rebellion

zones.text: the northern coastal towns from Surabaya to Cirebon

wars.outcome: The VOC and Mataram crushed the rebels; Kediri fell on 25 November 1678, Trunajaya surrendered on 26 December 1679, the lord of Giri was beaten in April 1680 and Puger was pardoned in November 1681.
wars.note: The page also names Bugis allies under Arung Palakka, Raden Kajoran (beaten at Mlambang in 1679) and a Cirebon that declared independence in 1677-1678 with Banten's support.

certainty.note: The page names towns, not boundaries; every region is a radius round a town or a chain of circles on Madura.

sources.title: Trunajaya rebellion
sources.note: Timeline of the rebel-held towns, Plered, Kediri, the VOC campaigns and the surrender.

notes: A rebel dossier written because Trunajaya's army held the Java north coast, Plered and Kediri for two years (September 1676 to November 1678); the single page opened (the Trunajaya rebellion article, counted in the Mataram budget) names towns but gives no boundaries and no date for the fall of the other coast towns, so the 1677 loss of Madura and the coast is confidence 1. Cliopatria has no row for the rebels, and its Mataram row has a gap 1677-1682. The lord of Giri (a Gresik polity that joined in early 1676 and was beaten in April 1680), the Makassarese under Karaeng Galesong and Pangeran Puger (who held Plered 1677-1680 and again August-November 1681) are not given dossiers: Giri and Puger are counterparts needing one if the project wants them. Madura is not a gazetteer region (a chain of circles stands in) and the coast excludes Jepara by leaving it out.
